text:
Alex: Heads-up — hit a weird production case this morning. Client retried after an early HTTP/2 103-like partial + trailers and ended up causing duplicate side-effects. Can we sync on a gateway contract for "finality" trailers and retry fencing?

Sam: Ugh, can you paste the minimal repro? 103? We normally do streaming, but we don't have a clear finality marker.

Alex: Minimal logs below — client saw data + a trailer header `rw-final: true` but our proxy sometimes proxies the retry upstream when the client replays from the start.

```
# simplified
CLIENT -> GATEWAY: request (no idempotency)
GATEWAY -> UPSTREAM: forwarded
UPSTREAM -> GATEWAY: partial response (stream data)
UPSTREAM -> GATEWAY: trailers { rw-final: true }
CLIENT: times out (network flake) and retries from start
GATEWAY: retries to UPSTREAM (duplicate side-effect)
```

Priya: Two orthogonal things here: (1) an explicit client-visible finality signal in trailers, and (2) gateway-local retry fencing so retries within a short window are deduped or turned into fast-fail. We should do both.

Taylor: Agreed. Also need to think about streaming vs non-streaming routes — long-running streams can't hold a retry lease forever (cost). We need bounded fencing windows.

Sam: Proposal sketch: per-route opt-in header that enables "trailer-finality + fence-token" semantics. Flow: upstream emits trailer `rw-final: true` + `rw-fence: <token>`. Gateway records token -> request-id mapping for TTL (e.g., 30s) and rejects duplicate upstream forward if retry contains same request fingerprint within window.

Alex: Example headers:
```
# client -> gateway
X-Client-Idempotency: <uuid>  # optional

# upstream -> gateway (trailer)
rw-final: true
rw-fence: 1234abcd
```

Priya: Implementation notes: gateway MUST NOT append a fence unless upstream provided it (we don't want to mutate contract silently). But gateway can refuse to forward a retry if it has the fence recorded for that (route,fingerprint). Also we should support gateway-generated fences when upstream can't provide them — in that case we have to make it explicit in the route config.

Taylor: Observability & billing: if we keep a 30s TTL per fence, high-rps routes could blow memory. Need sketched limits: per-tenant max fences, eviction policy LRU, and a fallback: if the fence store is full, gateway falls back to best-effort (log + metric) and forward as before.

Sam: Edge cases: what if upstream returns a fence but the client never sees it (gateway crashed before committing record)? We should persist fence metadata atomically with completion acknowledgement in the gateway to make it robust. For hosted mode that's doable; for private deployments we document best-effort and recommend idempotency keys.

Priya: Streaming nuance: for partial streaming responses where final trailer is delayed, we should support an interim trailer `rw-flush: true` and a terminal `rw-final`. Clients should treat only `rw-final` as finality.

Alex: Also propose a small change to retry semantics: gateway will add a wire-only header when it forwards a retry, e.g., `x-rw-retry-attempt: 2`, so upstreams can be aware and make side-effect decisions. This helps instrumenting.

Taylor: +1 for attempt header. We must ensure we strip it from responses and client-visible traces unless configured.

DevBot: Integration test run: gateway-fence-tests v2 — failing case is reproduced (test id=8421). Stack: gate v3.1.2.

Sam: Decision draft:
- New opt-in route flag: `enable_trailer_finality: boolean` (defaults false).
- Upstream MAY emit `rw-final` + `rw-fence`. If present, gateway records fence -> fingerprint (TTL default 30s).
- Gateway records must be durable in hosted mode for the window; in private mode documented as in-memory best-effort unless configured.
- Gateway will reject/short-circuit duplicate forwards if the fence mapping exists for incoming retry with matching fingerprint.
- Gateway will add `x-rw-retry-attempt` on forwarded retries.
- Metrics: `fence_record_count`, `fence_evictions`, `fence_forward_bypasses`.

Priya: Action items: I will prototype a calculation for fingerprint (route + idempotency header or body-hash) and a small LRU fence cache implementation.

Sam: I'll add integration tests simulating network flake + client replay and ensure we don't forward duplicate side-effect calls. Also add unit for `x-rw-retry-attempt` propagation.

Taylor: I'll mock load and estimate TTL vs memory for hot routes and propose default limits. Also add dashboard panels for `fence_evictions` and `fence_forward_bypasses`.

Alex: I'll update the RFC doc and add an example sequence diagram. Link to doc (WIP): https://redwood.internal/rfcs/gateway-fence (will push later). :thumbsup:

DevBot: Test run queued: fence-proto-PR (#782) by Priya. CI will run smoke + integration.

Sam: One more question — what about clients that legitimately need to retry because they didn't get any bytes at all? Our fingerprint should allow treating a zero-byte-ack as no side-effect and allow forward. So fingerprinting must consider observed bytes header or a flag.

Priya: Good point. We'll treat `observed_payload_bytes == 0` as not-final and not create fence records. Only create fence when upstream both emits `rw-final:true` and `observed_payload_bytes > 0` (configurable).

Taylor: Sounds reasonable. If this flows, we can roll as opt-in on a subset of routes and measure regressions.

Alex: Great sync. I'll spin up the RFC branch and ping infra for hosted durable store options. Meeting adjourned.

Sam: Thanks everyone.

Priya: PR incoming.

Taylor: Will follow up with dashboards.

DevBot: CI: fence-proto-PR started.
